So, the the overall theme is is called meta nature. When we life emerged from the primordial soup, we ate the soup until it was pretty much gone.

In the second energy crisis, peak oil and gas, synchronously, we discovered, invented photovoltaics.

Silicon is the octave of carbon in the periodic table, where matter can be seen as a puzzle that can only be assembled in certain ways. We life discovered how to assemble a set of solutions in biology, generally called nature.
There may be a parallel set of potential solutions that are just as elegant, inevitable, and constrained that life can only bring into being through humanity.
There are in turn solutions that humanity can only bring into being through silicon-based computation.
All of these are forms are bounded by and built into the puzzle that is matter.
A new realm of technologies that are emerging can be seen as an octave of nature. Solutions that are as elegant and inevitable as nature, but may only emerge through humanity and human technology.
This is analogous to an octave of nature.
Like nature, it may represent a potential plateau state when characterized by continued evolution within more and more highly optimized conditions for life.

This suggests that we are not separate from nature, but in some sense an extension of the same process whereby matter assembles itself into more and more complex structures conducive to greater complexity.
It suggests the possibility of a climax technology. A state as coherent and elegant as nature that can only be brought into being through humanity.
What has been described as the singularity, a log curve approaching an asymptote, might turn out to be the point of inflection in an S curve.
A curve that leads from nature to meta nature through the evolution of human technology.
The evolution of individual technologies are already well understood to follow S curves.
As each converges on the most efficient configuration of matter for that purpose, the system evolves toward what could ultimately be described as platonic solutions in matter.
At the point of inflection, change is so rapid that the curve appears to be vertical.

But as the efficiency of each fundamental technology tends towards the limits possible in matter, increasing the longevity of a technical solution provides greater return on the energy invested. At the far end of such evolution, technology might approach an extremely stable long-term plateau.
At the point of inflection, the system is so inefficient that it is necessarily sustainable and disposable.
But the mapping of matter to fundamental solutions is already beginning to be recognizable. As silicon is the octave of carbon in the periodic table, photovoltaics are the octave of photosynthesis.
Carbon remains not only the basis of biological life, but key in other forms from graphene to nanotubes.
Silicon is also the basis for computational structures to augment and extend human cognitive capabilities.
Lithium, the lightest element after hydrogen, has emerged as the basis for portable batteries.
Iron, at the center of the metals, is the cheapest, most abundant element for stationary long-term batteries.

Throughout material science, not only elements, but every possible combination is being revealed. This is unfolding even more rapidly with the help of AI. But this revelation only happens once for all of matter. Matter and energy in matter are a fundamental puzzle where the solution set is ultimately bounded.
Biology has evolved a domain of solutions that we call nature.

As human technology evolves at the quantum level, solutions approach approach that quality of coherent elegance. The deep coherence of the system may be apparent in patterns that can be described as resonant attractors.
Thus, we may begin to create parallel expressions of the same platonic potential that gave rise to nature.
